claims.statement: Capture and triage are deliberately split in time: `capture.capture()` lands raw text in `sources/` through the write path's immutable free-append fast path (committed immediately, zero organization demanded, no proposal in the moment), and `capture.triage()` later reuses the read-only `think` path over the capture to propose a placement, connections, and a grapple prompt without ever auto-moving or auto-filing the note.

A capture's write is scoped by `allowlist=["sources/"]`, and because its only change is a file absent at HEAD inside an append zone, `propose()` routes it to the free-append fast path: `commit_note()` lands it straight on HEAD and the result carries `fast_path=True` with `branch=None`, so the raw note is durable immediately with no proposal branch.

A capture's path is content-derived (`captures/<stamp>-<sha6>.md`, where `stamp` comes from the caller's `now` and defaults to the literal string `capture` when omitted, and `sha6` is the first six hex digits of the body's SHA-256), so re-capturing identical text re-derives an existing path; because the fast path applies only to files absent at HEAD, that second call resolves as an idempotent no-op rather than reaching an overwrite.

`hypermnesic capture <repo> <text>` is the CLI entrypoint for raw capture: it reports `{fast_path, files, commit}` (or the same as JSON), and it attaches an index handle only when `<repo>/.hypermnesic/index.db` already exists, which makes the index projection best-effort.

No capture tool is registered on the MCP surface: the read set is `search`, `hypermnesic_search`, `build_context`, `think`, `resolve`, `list_folders`, `read_note`, and `commit_note` is the only write tool, registered solely inside the `write_enabled` branch — so a remote client's low-friction raw landing goes through `commit_note` rather than a capture tool.

Triage derives its suggestion from thinking mode over the capture text: it keeps the first five related note paths excluding the capture itself, suggests the first related note's directory as placement with explicit `(undetermined — no close neighbours yet)` and `(vault root)` fallbacks, uses the first grounded question as the grapple prompt (with a fixed fallback), and proposes the rendered note at `dashboards/triage-<safe_slug(capture)>.md` under `allowlist=["dashboards/"]`.

Triage never moves, renames, or rewrites the capture and creates no branch when the capture path is missing; the proposal lands on a `hypermnesic/proposals/<slug>` branch, and the returned result carries `thought_wrote` — the thinking step's own `wrote` value — so the read-only proof is attached to the artifact instead of being a docstring promise.

`capture.backlog()` lists the raw captures without mutating them, reporting path, a whitespace-collapsed snippet capped at 200 characters, byte size, and a stage derived from whether `dashboards/triage-<slug>.md` exists in the live working tree; because proposal branches are committed in an isolated worktree, an unmerged triage proposal still reads `pending_triage`.

The capture backlog is composed into the daily-review surface as its `Capture backlog` section, while `capture.triage` is reachable only as a library call — the CLI exposes `capture` and `daily-review` subcommands, not triage.

Thinking mode's no-write boundary is structural and observable: the module imports only read surfaces (`retrieve`, `graph`, `ingest`) and cannot reach `commit_note` or `propose`, and `wrote` is always False and published by `as_dict()` so both the CLI JSON and the MCP tool result carry it.

The read-only boundary is enforced by the test suite, not just documented: a test scans the think module's import lines for `commit_note` and `propose`, other tests assert HEAD and the index path set are unchanged across a `think` call, and the read-only MCP tool set is asserted to be exactly the seven read tools with no write tool.

`think` reasons over distinct note paths rather than chunks: the Socratic prompt fires only when at least two distinct related notes exist and names both by resolved title (otherwise `questions` is empty), and unlinked pairs are computed over the top four distinct notes, capped at three, dropping any pair already joined by a wikilink.

Passing the active note's `path` excludes it from its own results, and when that exclusion removes every retrieval hit `think` falls back to the active note's graph neighbours as low-confidence `graph`-channel related notes at score 0.0 instead of returning a blank surface; a related note's display title is resolved from the file (with a stem fallback) rather than from the matched chunk's heading.

`think` degrades rather than failing: a no-match topic on the lexical channel returns empty `related` with a "nothing relevant yet" `note` and `wrote` still False, and dense unavailability is reported through `degraded_lexical_only`/`degraded_reason` taken from `retrieve.search`.

`folders.derive_folders()` is a pure function over the index's path set returning bounded folder entries `{path, writable, protected_reason, note_count}` with a recursive note count; writability is the write guard's verdict on a synthetic `__probe__.md` placed under the prefix (so a nested protected directory like `projects/scripts/` is correctly non-writable while its parent is writable); entries are sorted before the node cap so truncation drops a deterministic tail and reports `truncated`/`omitted`; depth is clamped to a ceiling.

Folder discovery and the write path share one coercion site: `build_server()` computes the effective write surface once and passes the same value to `commit_note`'s allowlist and to folder derivation, and the CLI `list-folders --allowlist` reuses that same helper so a preview matches the live write surface.

A malformed folder root fails closed rather than being normalized into something plausible: `normalize_root` rejects absolute paths and `..` traversal, the CLI exits non-zero with the message, and the MCP `list_folders` tool returns an empty, leak-free listing instead of an error a caller could probe with.

`agent_instruction` is the requested root's direct `AGENTS.md`, falling back to a direct `CLAUDE.md` only when `AGENTS.md` is absent, with descendant instruction files deliberately not aggregated; the content is sanitized before it leaves the remote read surface — host-local absolute paths become `<local-path>` and private/tailnet (or any `/mcp`) URLs become `<endpoint-url>` while repo-relative paths and public URLs survive.
Because folder paths come from the index's path set, skip directories are structurally undiscoverable rather than filtered by a second rule that could drift from the index's own exclusions.

Sidecar routing is keyed on extension and complexity — images and scanned, table-dense, or equation-bearing PDFs go to Docling; simple native PDFs and DOCX/PPTX/XLSX go to MarkItDown — with only permissive libraries in the `sidecar` extra and lazy extractor imports, and a conservative complexity probe that reads the first three pages, treats under 32 extractable characters as scanned, and returns an all-false default when the probe libraries or file are unusable.

`sidecar.needs_extraction()` re-extracts on exactly three conditions — no sidecar text, a `source_sha256` mismatch against the source bytes, or an `extractor_version` differing from the module's `EXTRACTOR_VERSION` — so an unchanged binary causes no churn, bumping the constant deliberately forces a corpus-wide re-extraction, and unparseable sidecar frontmatter counts as a mismatch.

`sidecar.build_sidecar()` is pure assembly: it routes, extracts through an injectable function, computes the hash and fidelity label, and renders the content-addressed provenance frontmatter in memory at `sidecars/<source_rel>.md` without writing anything, and `SIDECAR_DIR` is deliberately not a guard-protected directory.

Sidecar writes are proposals, never silent overwrites: `cold_start_proposal()` extracts a whole corpus into one batched proposal (not one per file, which would be the PR flood the global proposal budget bounds), and `reextract_proposal()` emits one review-gated proposal per changed source, both scoped to the `sidecars/` allowlist.

Every sidecar carries the `source: sidecar` trust tag, and `sidecar.trust_tag()` derives that label from either the path convention or that frontmatter key while returning `source` for everything else; the current posture accepts sidecar content and no code yet restricts sidecar-derived chunks from write-capable tools.

Extraction records an honest fidelity label — `low` when MarkItDown is used on a table-dense PDF, `partial` for `.xlsx` because flattening loses structure, otherwise `ok` — so a retrieved sidecar is not mistaken for a faithful copy.

What belongs in durable memory at all is governed by a taxonomy: five decision dimensions (duration, type, scope, update strategy, retrieval mode) plus explicit write / do-not-write lists, where durable project memory (semantic fact, episodic/source evidence, procedural or policy rule, generated summary that cites its sources, raw capture, current-state mirror) belongs and behavioural preference, temporary session state, transient personal inference, secrets, and unreviewed sensitive material do not.

Evidence-first is a workflow rule, not a style preference: preserve raw captures and cite source paths, never overwrite a raw capture with a cleaned summary (triage is allowed, silent source deletion is not), and route a genuine removal through the memory-control preview/apply flow so it becomes a new git event with audit context.

The engine only classifies memory after the fact: `memory_control._source_type` reports `generated` for a note carrying the generated marker, `captured` for any path under `sources/`, and `authored` otherwise, which is what backs `memory list --source-type captured` as a way to review raw intake.
